parts.text:
The Hidden Cost of Convenience

Over the past two decades, on-demand delivery services have transformed the way people shop, eat and manage their daily lives. What was once considered a luxury — having groceries, meals or even medication delivered within the hour — has become an expectation for a growing segment of the population. Yet behind this apparent convenience lies a complex web of economic and social trade-offs that are only now beginning to receive serious attention.

Proponents argue that such services free up valuable time, particularly for those juggling demanding careers and family responsibilities. Critics, however, point to the precarious working conditions faced by many delivery workers, who often lack the job security and benefits afforded to traditional employees. Moreover, the environmental impact of increased packaging and vehicle emissions remains a contentious issue that companies have been slow to address.
